sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A deciduous, dioecious tree native to China, usually 5–20 m tall and sometimes about 35 m. It is widely planted beyond its natural range.

sections.title: Leaves and reproduction
sections.text: The fan-shaped leaves have veins that fork repeatedly. Male trees produce pollen in catkins; female trees bear naked seeds about 1–2 cm long, surrounded by a fleshy, odorous outer covering. That covering is not a botanical fruit.

sections.title: Toxicity
sections.text: The seeds contain toxic compounds. Serious poisonings have been reported from raw seeds and even after roasting; consumption is not recommended.
